articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently naming vulnerabilities after 80s sci-fi is how we cope with existential dread now. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year, which is either impressive vigilance or deeply concerning.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence is mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens by exploiting ancient router vulnerabilities. The fact that people are still running ancient routers in 2026 is the real national security threat here.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets pwned by ransomware crew, disrupting education nationwide because apparently holding students' futures hostage is the new black. Nothing says 'digital transformation' quite like your LMS being held for ransom.

articles.title: US bank reports itself after slinging customer data at 'unauthorized AI app'
articles.summary: DOJ now treats FOIA dodging as a crime worthy of arrest and strip searches — stunning hypocrisy from an administration that perfected the art of records stonewalling. Rules for thee, but not for we, apparently.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Apple finally enables end-to-end encryption for RCS cross-platform messaging after years of green bubble segregation. Your Android friends can now send you encrypted disappointment instead of plain text disappointment.

articles.title: Hugging Face Packages Weaponized With a Single File Tweak
articles.summary: EFF fights for warrant requirements on border device searches at the Fourth Circuit, because apparently the Constitution gets fuzzy at customs. Your phone shouldn't be fair game just because you decided to leave the country.

articles.title: Google says it likely thwarted effort by hacker group to use AI for 'mass exploitation event'
articles.summary: Google spots hackers using AI to hunt zero-days for mass exploitation — the singularity isn't coming, it's already here and it's filing CVEs. This is allegedly just 'the tip of the iceberg,' so sleep well tonight.

articles.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
articles.summary: Mini Shai-Hulud worm compromises TanStack, Mistral AI, and other major packages in fresh supply chain carnage. TeamPCP continues their npm reign of terror, proving that the spice must flow, even if it's malicious.

articles.title: New TrickMo Variant Uses TON C2 and SOCKS5 to Create Android Network Pivots
articles.summary: RubyGems suspends new signups after hundreds of malicious packages flood the ecosystem in coordinated attack. The gem mine is temporarily closed while they sweep for explosives.

articles.title: How Open Source Dependency and Repo Attacks Compromise DevOps Pipelines and How to Stay Safe
articles.summary: Nine-year-old 'Dirty Frag' vulnerability finally surfaces, enabling root access on Linux systems with public PoC exploit code. Nothing quite like a decade-old privilege escalation bug to remind us that legacy code is the gift that keeps on giving.
